report.source_text: A histologic evaluation of a biopsy specimen of the largest nodule revealed an inflammatory, granulomatous-diffuse infiltrate in the superficial and deep dermis consisting of giant cells, histiocytes, lymphocytes, neutrophils, eosinophils, and plasma cells (Figure 1). The Ziehl–Neelsen and Gram stains were both negative. The cultures for the anaerobic and aerobic bacteria, fungi, and acid-fast bacilli were negative, as they were the antibody tests for Bartonella henselae and Afipia felis.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 3-year-old girl presented with a 2-month history of progressive, asymptomatic nodules on the left cheek that were refractory to systemic amoxicillin-clavulanate. Physical examination revealed two non-fluctuant, hard-elastic nodules (1cm and 2cm) with overlying erythema but negative thermotouch, without lymphadenopathy or fever. Ultrasound demonstrated homogenous, hypoechoic, solid lesions consistent with granulomatous rather than cystic or infectious pathology. Histopathological evaluation of a biopsy specimen revealed a diffuse granulomatous infiltrate consisting of giant cells, histiocytes, lymphocytes, neutrophils, eosinophils, and plasma cells. Microbiological workup including Ziehl-Neelsen and Gram stains, cultures for aerobic/anaerobic bacteria, fungi, and acid-fast bacilli, and serology for Bartonella henselae and Afipia felis were all negative, confirming the 'aseptic' nature. Based on these findings, IFAG was suspected and treatment with topical fusidic acid and oral clarithromycin was initiated for 14 days. The lesions resolved completely after two months with no recurrence at three-month follow-up.
